title: Snake Game Logic
description: Snake on a w x h grid. Maintain the body as a queue of cells plus a Set for O(1) self-collision lookup. Each move: compute the new head, drop the tail UNLESS the new cell eats food, then check walls and self-overlap.

notes: Drop the tail BEFORE checking self-overlap — otherwise legal moves that occupy the old tail cell falsely register as collisions.
Track body cells in a Set keyed by 'r,c' for O(1) collision lookup; the array gives ordered queue semantics.
Food is a queue (FIFO) — only the FRONT food piece is eligible. Compare head's new cell against food[0] only.

questions.q: Why store the body in a Set in addition to an array?
options: O(1) self-collision check; the array preserves order for tail removal
Sets are required by the rules

questions.q: When the snake eats food, what changes vs a regular move?
options: The tail is NOT removed, so the snake grows by one

questions.q: Why remove the tail before the self-collision check?
options: Otherwise moving into the old tail cell would falsely flag as a collision
Sets do not support delete after lookup

questions.q: What does move return on a wall or self crash?

exercises.prompt: Fill in Snake.move so a 3x3 grid with food at [0,1] yields score 1 after eating, then -1 on the wall.

L3.prompt: Build Snake(width, height, food) with move(dir) returning new score or -1 on crash. On a 3x3 grid with one food at [0,1], run R, R, U. Logs: 1, 1, -1.
hints: Body array's last element is the head; the first element is the tail.
Drop the tail BEFORE the self-collision check unless the new cell ate food.
Track body cells in a Set keyed by 'r,c' for O(1) collision lookup.
